prior_findings_note: P1-P11 and N1-N13 were NOT reopened or rewritten. Sol's N11/N12/N13 observations confirm those repairs stand. Edits outside P12/P13 are limited to the coupled baseline-citation strings in tasks .1/.3/.4/.5/.6/.7 that P13 makes durable.

P12.finding: The metrics contract could not support its own assertions: it was described as timestamped event names and explicitly as 'counters only, no payloads', while P-3/P-4b require correlating each renderStart/renderCancel/renderSettle to a specific page, render task, and generation. The append-only global stream was also unbounded despite the feature's bounded-memory intent.
P12.resolution: The spec gains a dedicated 'Metrics channel contract' section defining one executable schema, and every 'counters only / no payloads' contradiction is explicitly superseded there and reworded in task .2 and task .3. Each record carries: seq (per-channel monotonic, never reused - the total order all ordering assertions use), t (performance.now(), with one channel-level t0Epoch), docId (opaque per-getDocument instance counter; two loads of the same file differ), pageNumber (null for document-scoped events), taskId (opaque per-RenderTask counter, channel-unique), genId (monotonic per docId, bumped on every zoom/fit/scale commit; a task's cancel and settle repeat its start's genId), kind, outcome (completed|cancelled|failed, only on renderSettle), scale (logical), and canvasWidth/canvasHeight (post-DPR/area-cap backing-store dims). Identifiers are opaque in-process counters, never derived from URL, path, URI, filename, or title, and no field carries document text - task .2 adds a privacy unit assertion using distinctive fixture path and title strings. Invariants: exactly one terminal renderSettle per renderStart taskId (never zero, never two); renderCancel at most once per taskId, after its start and before its settle, whose outcome is 'cancelled'; taskId channel-unique with (docId, pageNumber, genId) correlating task to page and generation; genId non-decreasing, and a replacement generation's first renderStart has strictly greater seq than the superseded generation's renderCancel and renderSettle(cancelled) - exactly P-4b. Retention: bounded ring buffer (~2000 events default) that increments a visible 'dropped' counter instead of growing, so truncation can never be misread as 'nothing happened'; reset({capacity}) clears records/dropped/sequence and may raise capacity for a QA run; snapshot() returns a frozen structural clone plus {capacity, dropped, seqHigh, t0Epoch} without mutating or truncating the live buffer; export() yields the JSON-serializable evidence form. Task .6 adds a metrics-channel run protocol applying to every P-3/P-4/P-6 window: reset with ample capacity before the window, measure from snapshot(), assert dropped === 0 on every snapshot used for an assertion (non-zero invalidates the measurement and forces a re-run, never a pass), correlate by docId/pageNumber/taskId/genId ordered by seq, and export each window verbatim into the artifact. P-3 now counts starts scoped to the document instance from a dropped === 0 snapshot with exactly-one-terminal-settle; P-6 scopes documentDestroy and post-navigation silence to the docId. Unit acceptance added in task .2 (schema conformance, seq/t monotonicity, opaque ids, privacy, ring-buffer/dropped/reset/snapshot/export) and task .3 (correlation from the hooks, exactly-one-terminal-settle with no orphans, cancel -> cancelled-settle -> replacement-start ordering, retention/reset behavior under churn).

P13.finding: The clean baseline lived only under /tmp/fn112-baseline/ with no durable manifest, hashes, environment metadata, or regeneration path, leaving later comparisons and the final R17 receipt unverifiable across tasks and sessions.
P13.resolution: Task .2 step 0 still captures the baseline BEFORE any dependency or product edit (rule unchanged), but now writes a durable in-repository receipt .flow/reviews/fn-112-baseline-receipt.json (plus a human-readable .md) in the same step; /tmp raw logs are explicitly scratch. The receipt is a Flow evidence artifact only: under .flow/reviews/, not product code, in no files array, imported by nothing, covered by no product test. Per command it records the exact command string, exit status, duration, parsed pass/fail counts, the ENUMERATED pre-existing failure list (test names + messages), the raw log's sha256, and its path; top-level it records base_sha bb994b580356a41a31093fea85b06993c1a18e4c, branch feat/native-pdf-renderer, a clean-worktree flag, bun --version, bunx tsc --version, platform/arch/uname, ISO-8601 started_at/finished_at, and environment notes. Regeneration: if the raw logs vanish or hash-mismatch, the baseline is regenerated deterministically via git worktree add --detach <tmpdir> bb994b580356a41a31093fea85b06993c1a18e4c, bun install --frozen-lockfile inside that worktree only (never mutating the working tree's node_modules or lockfile), the same four commands, then git worktree remove; the result is APPENDED as a new captures[] entry with regenerated: true and its reason - the original entry is never edited or deleted, and any divergence in the failure list is recorded rather than overwritten. R17 now states the comparison rule explicitly: the final gate diffs its failures against the named list in the cited captures[] entry, a failure absent from that list is a new failure and blocks, the completion evidence cites the receipt path and the exact capture_id, and a missing or unverifiable receipt means R17 is not yet satisfiable. Task .7's final gate and its acceptance items were updated to that citation form, and the baseline citations in tasks .1/.3/.4/.5/.6 now point at the durable receipt instead of the /tmp path. Nothing was executed: no baseline run, no worktree, no install - this is the plan for it.

consistency_audit.r17_final_gate: Task .7's approach bullet and both acceptance lists require comparing against the receipt's enumerated failure list and citing the receipt path plus capture_id, with the worktree regeneration fallback.
